{"n":25,"title":"fix: eliminate disabled-watchdog cold-start scans","merged":true,"body":"## Summary

- remove eager Git worktree fingerprinting from watchdog construction and session binding
- gate repository signatures on the effective main-watchdog enablement state
- lazily establish the repo-edit baseline at the first relevant `before_agent_start`
- clear signature state across session and disable boundaries
- add regression coverage for disabled startup, enabled change review, pre-existing dirty files, and session rebinding

## Root cause

`MainWatchdogRuntime` computed the complete repository change signature in its constructor, then twice more while binding the initial session. This happened even though the main watchdog is disabled by default. The signature invokes Git status and stats/hashes dirty paths, so Windows cold filesystem, Defender, and OneDrive state could turn deferred subagent attachment into a multi-second first-prompt delay.

The fix removes all constructor/session-bind scans. An enabled repo-edit watchdog now fingerprints once at turn start and once at agent end, preserving the existing rule that only edits made during that turn trigger review.

## Verification

- focused Vitest regression set: 25/25 passed
- required tsgo build sequence passed: tui, ai, agent, coding-agent, orchestrator
- touched-file Biome passed; the vendored watchdog source remains excluded by repository configuration
- dirty-worktree startup benchmark: prompt-ready 2.23s, deferred attach 265ms, `pi-subagents` factory 6ms

The full coding-agent suite was also attempted: 2236 tests passed and 125 failed in unrelated current-master/Windows areas; no watchdog test failed. Full Biome reports 35 existing errors and one warning outside the touched files.

## Out of scope

The larger first-paint ESM/TypeBox module graph remains a secondary cold-cache amplifier. This PR intentionally does not refactor that graph or the startup profiler; it fixes only the experimentally isolated default-off watchdog scan.

{"n":23,"title":"release: v0.2.11 same-turn swarm, gateway /new, cron allowlist","merged":true,"body":"## Summary
- Same-turn SINGLE `subagent` calls count toward the swarm gate. One once/reject covers that assistant message. Same-turn singles overlap; sequential work stays `chain`.
- Gateway `/new` while busy aborts the live turn and drops the queue.
- TUI cron uses the same deliver allowlist as the gateway. Delivery also refuses a persisted chat that is not home/allowed/origin.
- Corrupt models-store JSON is treated as empty.
- Plan-mode git walk skips known globals. Manual mode prompts for apply-mode `code_rewrite`.

## Test plan
- [x] permissions, plan-mode, models-store, gateway-cron, gateway-router, gateway-agent-bridge, subagent-permission-inherit
- [ ] After merge: tag `v0.2.11` so `publish-npm.yml` ships `@ashx-j/lunr@0.2.11`"}
{"n":22,"title":"release: v0.2.10 image chips, subagent TUI, grok Responses","merged":true,"body":"## Summary
- Clipboard paste inserts `[image_n]` chips and attaches `ImageContent` on submit; `/edit` restores chips + files.
- VS Code Alt+V / leaked `ESC v` image paste on win32.
- Quieter subagent compact rows (tools · tokens · time), unlimited parallel defaults, independent footer TPS toggle.
- grok-4.5+ uses Responses via a version floor (`parseXaiGrok4Minor >= 5`), not a frozen id. grok-4.6+ keeps native xhigh.

## Test plan
- [x] `packages/ai`: xai-thinking + xai-responses
- [x] `packages/coding-agent`: image-paste-markers, subagent compact/parallel, thinking-tail, tool-execution, model-refresh-merge (after ai rebuild)
- [x] TUI editor + keys image-chip tests are in the tree (full tui suite still hits Win32 symlink EPERM on autocomplete)
- [ ] After merge: tag `v0.2.10` so `publish-npm.yml` ships `@ashx-j/lunr@0.2.10`

Not in this cut: same-turn SINGLE swarm gate; gateway `/new` while busy; cron deliver allowlist; models-store corrupt JSON parse."}
{"n":21,"title":"release: v0.2.9 behavior presets and product UX","merged":true,"body":"Lockstep 0.2.9.

Ships:
- Behavior presets (#20)
- Product UX (#19): lunr tab title, Orchestrating spinner, fresh-only advertised subagents, per-tier thinking, lunr update, git/plan footer (plan bar can be hidden independently of the percent), click-to-expand

{"n":19,"title":"feat: product UX (title, orchestrating, update, git/plan footer, click-expand)","merged":true,"body":"lunR product UX for 0.2.9.

- Orchestrating... spinner text while subagents run
- Hide fork context from the model; children always start fresh
- Per-tier thinking levels
- lunr update CLI + startup version notice (workspace npx skips)

- Footer plan usage bar with 5h/weekly setting; Customize can hide the segment or hide only the bar and keep the percent
- Click thinking/tool cards to expand; drop global ctrl+o (tree filter keeps ctrl+o)

Does not include behavior presets (separate PR)."}
{"n":18,"title":"v0.2.8: OpenCode Zen free models + TUI bug fixes","merged":true,"body":"## Summary
Merge the two unmerged product branches onto master for npm 0.2.8.

- **feat/opencode-zen-free-models:** generate-models intersects live OpenCode Zen `/v1/models` (and Go) with models.dev. Catalog JSON regenerated at merge. OpenCode Go now registers the Responses API for live rows that use it.

{"n":2,"title":"feat(agent): agent-swarm approval gate for auto-activated parallel fan-out","merged":false,"body":"## What

An auto-activated agent swarm — one `subagent` tool call launching **more than 2 parallel subagents** — now requires user approval in **manual and yolo** modes. Only `auto` mode bypasses the gate. Explicit `/swarm` turns are pre-approved (the user already asked for the swarm).

TUI dialog:

```
▶ Approve AgentSwarm?

agent swarm (4 subagents)
Explore lunR auth/model/settings/plan systems

  1. Approve once
  2. Approve for this session
  3. Reject
  4. Reject with feedback
```

Reject-with-feedback collects a one-line reason that becomes the block reason the model sees, so it can adjust the plan. On approval the footer shows `swarm ● active` for the rest of the turn, same as an explicit /swarm.

## How

- `core/swarm.ts`: `SWARM_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD` (2), `effectiveSwarmCount` (tasks[] with `count` multipliers + chain `parallel` blocks; dynamic `expand` fan-out has no static count and is not gated), `isExplicitSwarmTurn` (last user message starts with `[SWARM MODE]` — works for TUI + gateway since both inject the same prompt).
- `core/permissions.ts`: swarm branch in `gateToolCall` runs before the mode early-return so yolo is gated too; `ApprovalResponse` is now decision strings OR `{ decision: "reject", feedback }`; `ApprovalRequest.kind?: "swarm"`; session approval under the `"swarm"` action key; fail-closed without a handler.
- `agent-session.ts`: computes `explicitSwarmTurn` from the branch, passes via new `GateOptions`.
- TUI: `showSwarmApprovalDialog`; `ExtensionSelectorComponent` gains 1-9 number-key selection (all selectors).
- Gateway: AgentSwarm prompt title; buttons stay once/session/reject — inline buttons can't capture free text, so reject-with-feedback is TUI-only.

## Verification

- `permissions.test.ts` grew to 26 tests (swarm count helpers, mode matrix, explicit-swarm exemption, session approval, reject-feedback reason, fail-closed) — all pass
- `gateway-approval.test.ts` (6) passes
- Build agent → coding-agent → orchestrator all exit 0; `biome check packages/` clean; `npx lunr --print` smoke responds

Interactive dialog flow not live-tested in this environment.

I count a named model as attribution even when the author wrote “Grok 4.5” rather than a provider-qualified `provider/model` slug. This makes the useful inclusion rule **Grok-attributed or no identifiable model attribution**. For transparency, only five bodies contain a provider-qualified slash slug: #91, #92, #94, #95, and #96. ### Complete qualifying inventory

- **42 with no identifiable model attribution in the body or issue comments:** **[#1](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/1)–[#34](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/34)** inclusive, plus **[#97](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/97), [#98](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/98), [#104](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/104), [#105](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/105), [#112](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/112)–[#115](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/115)**. The other 46 have non-Grok model attribution.

These groups are disjoint. **Missing attribution says nothing about whether tests ran.** In particular, #1 reports a local `npm audit` result of **zero vulnerabilities**; my earlier missing-test characterization of it was wrong.

| Priority | PR and disposition | Evidence gap; worthwhile check |
|---|---|---|

| High | [#96, Telegram/Discord continuation](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/96), merged | **398 tests** and a compiled local gateway check are recorded. Live bot interactions and native service install/reboot remain explicitly unverified. Limit follow-up to those host-level scenarios. |

Test those two flows with authorization; do not repeat its service-tier unit suite. |
| Medium | [#19, product UX](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/19), merged, missing attribution | Broad runtime changes, including update checks, footer data and fresh-child behavior, have **no execution result in this PR body**. This is missing PR-level evidence, not proof of no tests. Later focused product UX and release coverage exists. Check only a surviving behavior that those tests missed. |

Later subagent-row PRs and their focused tests cover much of this display path. Review current tier-versus-explicit-model labeling rather than replaying #38’s branch. |
| Low, attribution-required | [#24, swarm approval normalization](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/24), merged, missing attribution | One-paragraph publish fix has **no recorded test execution in its body**. Later permission and combined release suites provide stronger evidence. Only check sibling SINGLE-call approval caching if those suites lack that case. |

Several apparent gaps should **not** generate active-code retests. Grok-filed [#60](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/60) added an empty-chat context card that [#68](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/68) removed; #68 then shipped through [#69](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/69)’s recorded checks. [#72](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/72) lacks a count in its body, but the repository’s `AGENTS.md` records passing continuation tests, and [#80](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/80) records combined subagent testing. [#86](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/86) records **185 focused tests**, builds, first-turn and package checks; #87 only documents its publication. The later release PRs #104, #112 and #113 also record combined validation despite having no model attribution.

Among unmerged work, **[#2](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/2), [#28](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/28), [#61](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/61)** qualify, but #28 was superseded by tested [#30](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/30), #61 by tested #62/#63, and #2’s old swarm contract should not be tested as current code.
